newsitem.title: USA: Conn.governor seeks nonresident gambler tax - report.
newsitem.headline: Conn.governor seeks nonresident gambler tax - report.

text.p: Connecticut Governor John Rowland is asking state lawmakers to enact a tax on the gambling winnings of out-of-state bettors, the Hartford Courant reported on Tuesday.
Connecticut has two of the world's three biggest casinos, operated by the Mashantucket Pequot and the Mohegan Indians respectively.
Rowland, a Republican, estimates that the new tax could generate $6 million in the first year of the two-year budget and $12 million in the second year, the report said.
But the difficulty in collecting more money is rooted in state and federal regulations.
There is presently no mechanism to tax anyone who wins less than $600.
Another problem is that many casino customers end up losing money, and so owe no tax at all.
